title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Unsolved Indiana Dunes Disappearances
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the 1966 disappearance of three young women—Patricia Blow, Anne Miller, and Renee Brule—who vanished on Saturday, July 2, 1966, at Indiana Dunes State Park on Lake Michigan near Chicago. The episode covers the last sightings, the abandoned belongings and Buick, the large land, sea, and air search, the letter found in Brule's purse, the women's links to a horse stable run by organized crime figure Silas Jane, the boat sightings (a white Tryhold runabout with turquoise interior and a cabin cruiser with a sanded-off name), boat wreckage, a psychic's clue, and the main theories (drowning, the Dick Wiley abortion theory involving the Largo family, a Silas Jane revenge theory, the brother's faked-disappearance theory, and Richard Speck). A listener mail segment closes the episode.
topics: Stuff You Should Know true crime playlist

segments.title: Cold open
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Indiana Dunes disappearance of three women in July 1966 as a sad, unresolved true crime case.

segments.title: Opening banter and preamble
segments.summary: Hosts joke about spin-off TV shows and mysteries, then discuss the boat type and set up the case.
topics: Stuff You Should Know true crime playlist

segments.title: The women and their last sighting
segments.summary: Patricia Blow, Anne Miller, and Renee Brule drive to Indiana Dunes State Park on Saturday July 2, 1966. They set up on the beach, go into the water around noon, and the last sighting is by a teenage couple who notice their belongings left behind. A park ranger collects the items.

segments.title: Missing person report and abandoned belongings
segments.summary: Harold Blow calls the ranger station that evening about his missing daughter. Rangers find the Buick and state police take over. The women left wallets, a transistor radio, magazines, and suntan lotion behind, which seems suspicious.

segments.title: Search effort
segments.summary: A large land, sea, and air search includes soldiers, the Civil Air Patrol, the Coast Guard, dive teams, and a sheriff's posse. Critics note the search began two days after the women vanished, and it found nothing.

segments.title: Renee Brule's letter and Anne Miller's pregnancy
segments.summary: A letter in Brule's purse suggested she wanted to leave her marriage, but her husband and family denied marital trouble and police cleared him. Anne Miller was reportedly about three months pregnant and may have been dating a married man. Patty was also reportedly dating a married man.

segments.title: Silas Jane and the horse stable
segments.summary: Anne and Patty rode horses at a stable linked to Silas Jane, a violent criminal and organized crime figure. Anne also worked there as a horse exerciser. Police saw this as a major red flag.

segments.title: Boat sightings and wreckage
segments.summary: A couple from Indianapolis reported the women leaving with a tanned, dark-haired man in a white Tryhold runabout with turquoise interior. Another witness reported them on a cabin cruiser with three men around 3 pm, and that boat's name had been sanded off. Boat wreckage washed ashore but no boat was reported wrecked that weekend.

segments.title: Home movies and the boat that was never found
segments.summary: Home movies filmed on the beach seemed to show the three women on the runabout, and the cabin cruiser was largely ruled out. Police circulated the boat description, but it was never found.

segments.title: Harold Blow's vigil and the psychic clue
segments.summary: Harold Blow kept searching for the rest of his life, including private reconnaissance flights. A psychic described a cabin on Lake Michigan with a rotted lawn chair. Police found a cabin matching the description nine years later, but digging found nothing.

segments.title: Drowning theory and swimming ability
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the women being strong swimmers and that drowning is possible given Lake Michigan's dangers, though bodies usually surface.

segments.title: Dick Wiley's abortion theory and the Largo family
segments.summary: Crime reporter Dick Wiley theorized Anne Miller went for an illegal abortion on a houseboat, which turned fatal. He linked it to Frank and Helen Largo, who ran an illegal abortion clinic in Gary, Indiana, and to their nephew Ralph, who resembled the boat driver. The hosts find the theory unlikely.

segments.title: Silas Jane revenge theory and unverified insurance claim
segments.summary: One theory says the women witnessed a car bombing linked to Silas Jane and were killed. An associate resembled the boat driver, and an unverified rumor says he filed an insurance claim for a boat that sank.

segments.title: Faked disappearance theory and Richard Speck
segments.summary: Patty Blow's brother posted on Websleuths suggesting the women staged their disappearance to escape danger, and the helper turned out to be connected to Silas Jane. Some suggest a serial killer picked them up, but the hosts doubt Richard Speck, who had killed eight nursing students in Chicago on July 13, 1966.

segments.title: Resources and transition
segments.summary: Hosts suggest reading the Chicago Tribune article, the Northwest Indiana Times, Websleuths, and other resources, then move to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail from Katherine in Chicago
segments.summary: Katherine, a listener recently divorced and co-parenting, says the show helps her feel less lonely on kid-free days. Hosts thank her and give contact info.
